title: SportsCapping Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: SportsCapping review, checked 17 Nov 2026: a 76 handicapper pick marketplace, prices from $25 picks to $199 a month, how the replacement guarantee works.
dek: A pick marketplace that says it has sold picks since 2003 and lists 76 handicappers. Single picks on the 17 Nov 2026 board cost $25 to $59.99, and a Monthly Club runs $199 a month. Losing guaranteed packages earn a free replacement package, not cash, and every record on the site is graded by SportsCapping itself.

short_answer: SportsCapping is a real, working marketplace. On 17 Nov 2026 its board listed 382 picks from 62 handicappers, prices were posted for every package, and the FAQ names Boyd Information Group as the company that bills buyers. In that narrow sense it is legitimate.

Whether its handicappers make money for buyers is a different question. The site says "Every pick is documented, every record is verified," but the grading is done by SportsCapping, the company that earns money on every sale. The leaderboards on the homepage lead with windows such as yesterday, the last 7 days and the last 30 days, where a large roster always has someone on a hot run.

Buyer feedback is small and mostly negative: App Store reviews from 2015 to 2025 complain about losing picks and slow email support, with two positive reviews, and one 2026 BBB complaint about a season pass that was charged but not switched on, later resolved. If you buy, buy short, log every pick yourself and judge a handicapper over hundreds of plays.

guarantee: The About page says: "If a guaranteed package doesn't profit, you automatically get the next day of picks free; guaranteed subscriptions extend for the same length." The FAQ adds that no claim is needed and the make good is applied to your account on its own. A guarantee badge shows on each package that has one.

That is a replacement, not a refund. It never covers the money lost on the bets themselves, which is usually far more than the pick price. On cash refunds the FAQ says only that "refunds are reviewed individually" and asks buyers to contact support. The Terms of Use say the site and its content are provided "as is" and "for entertainment purposes", that disputes go to courts in Iowa, and that any claim must be filed within one year.

claims_note: The site states its own method: records cover each handicapper's premium picks, and figures labelled "Best Run" or "since" a date show a window that starts on the date shown, "not a lifetime record." That is an honest label, and it also tells you the headline numbers are chosen slices.

Some listings are more candid than most in this business. The featured Rocky Atkinson pack on 17 Nov 2026 showed "5 of 19 winning weeks" in college basketball next to a 14-7 record for the last 30 days. Reading both numbers side by side is the right habit for every handicapper on the site.
Profit is shown in dollars on $100 bets. The pages we read did not say whether that figure is net of the price of the picks, which a buyer pays on top.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing we could find. We found no full, time stamped pick log kept by an outside party and no monitoring service result for the marketplace as a whole.

What SportsCapping publishes: the FAQ says every pick is graded automatically against final scores and that a full history is on each handicapper profile. The handicapper pages we opened show a free pick with its line, odds and time of entry. All of this is kept by the company that sells the picks.

The same grading appears on BetFirm, a sister storefront whose leaderboard uses the SportsCapping "Sc Score" column and whose buy buttons go to the SportsCapping cart. Those numbers are not a second, independent check.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no SportsCapping handicapper is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these handicappers perform.
our_data.context: For scale: SportsCapping leaderboards feature runs such as 5-0 yesterday or 64.7% over 7 days. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on SportsCapping is thin. The main pool is 10 App Store reviews of the SportsCapping app from 2015 to 2025 and one BBB complaint from 2026. CapperTek has no reviews. The Reddit search for this page was partial: the Arctic Shift archive's full text search timed out for most queries on 17 Nov 2026, so we used a local copy of earlier Reddit downloads and the few queries that did return. Unhappy buyers are the likeliest to write, so this shows what goes wrong for some buyers, not how many.

customers.text: We found 11 buyer posts across two places. Of 10 App Store reviews from 2015 to 2025, seven are negative (one of them a sarcastic five star review): users say the paid picks lost, that the posted stats did not match their own results, that a free replacement for a losing guaranteed package also lost, and that support was by email only. Two are positive (a long time customer praising a support staffer, and a short 2017 rave) and one, from 2016, is a neutral first impression. One BBB complaint in 2026 said a paid season pass was never switched on; the company fixed it and offered a refund. No buyer posted a tracked record either way.
A one star App Store reviewer warned against buying. They said a losing package is replaced with another package that can also lose, so the buyer is out both the pick price and the bets.
A one star reviewer said support by email did not solve their problems, complained that there is no phone number, and recommended a different handicapper instead.
A five star reviewer said they have used SportsCapping for many years and found a member of the support team very helpful.
A five star review that is sarcastic in substance: "Just fade every pick." The reviewer said betting against the picks had paid well.

Three reviews say the same thing in different words: one user tracked the picks at 1 and 10 after following them, one tested the experts and lost a lot, and one said the experts are poor and their stats do not add up.
A five star reviewer called the app's selections the best in the world. The review gives no detail or record.

A BBB complaint said a $399.95 season pass bought on 5 Sep 2026 was charged but not delivered, and that several emails went unanswered. The business replied that a system fault left the pass inactive, that it switched the pass on dated back to the purchase, and that it offered a partial or full refund. BBB lists the complaint as resolved.
The only Reddit post our archive search found that names SportsCapping is a handicapper's own free play post linking to his SportsCapping profile. It is promotion, not a buyer review.

CapperTek lists SportsCapping.com with no reviews or complaints. Our partial Reddit archive search found no buyer discussion of the marketplace, and web searches found no Sportsbook Review, Covers or TheRX thread reviewing it. We did not read Trustpilot.

conflicts: SportsCapping grades and publishes the records of the handicappers it sells and earns money on every sale. The About page invites handicappers to "start earning commission on every pick you sell." The scorekeeper and the store are the same company.

The same platform supplies other storefronts. BetFirm sends its buyers to the SportsCapping cart with an affiliate code in the link. Rankings that appear on one site are not an outside check on another.
strengths: Every price is posted, and the cheapest picks start at $25.
Guarantees are applied automatically, with no claim to file.
The site labels its "since" and "Best Run" windows as windows, not lifetime records, and some listings show losing week counts.
A BBB complaint in 2026 was answered and resolved with a refund offer.
concerns: All records are graded by the company that sells the picks. No outside monitor found.
The guarantee is a replacement package or extra time, never cash, and refunds are case by case.
Homepage leaderboards lead with yesterday, 7 day and 30 day windows.
Most of the buyer reviews we found were negative, though the sample is small.
Support is by email or ticket; reviewers and the BBB complainant said they could not find a phone number.
checklist: Open the handicapper's full history, not the leaderboard window, and count every pick for the last 12 months.
Count units and dollars, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Remember the guarantee is more picks from the same handicapper, not your money back.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner.
faq: It is a real marketplace that delivers the picks it sells, posts every price and names Boyd Information Group as the company behind it. We could not verify that its handicappers win over time, because every record is graded by SportsCapping itself.

On 17 Nov 2026 single picks and small packs cost $25 to $59.99, a weekend of football picks from one handicapper cost $99, and the Monthly Club cost $199 a month. Long passes for top names ran up to $1,999.95 for a year.
Not in cash. A losing guaranteed package earns a free replacement package or extra time, applied automatically. The FAQ says refunds are reviewed case by case, and credits cannot be cashed out.

Only if a handicapper's full history, not a hot window, shows a profit over hundreds of picks after the price of the picks. At -110 odds you need about 52.4% just to break even, and nothing we found independently confirms that any SportsCapping handicapper clears it.
